data.markdown:
# Bifrost Attachments - storage message types

Read and write files in external storage (Azure Blob Storage, Azure File Share or SharePoint) through the Business Central external file storage connectors, stage large files in chunks and keep document attachments in storage instead of the database.

Storage file writes refuse an existing destination by default. Send overwrite: true only to intentionally replace an unlinked file. Copy and Move always refuse an existing destination. CreateForRecord and CreateLinked link pre-existing storage files without acquiring deletion ownership: Restore and attachment deletion preserve those files.

## Getting started

1. Call `Storage.Account.List` to see the storage connections set up on the Attachments Setup page. Each row has a `storageCode`.
2. Send that `storageCode` with every other storage call. Paths are relative to the base folder of the connection and use forward slashes; `.` and `..` segments, backslashes and double slashes are refused.
3. Read the full contract of one type with `Help.Implementation.Get` (subject = the message type).
Storage operations use the registered Business Central External File Storage connector interface. Attachments does not select behavior from connector IDs or inspect connector-owned account tables, and it requires no minimum connector version or build: any connector registered with External File Storage works. The registered connector owns credentials, provider-specific path rules and backend errors. Attachments validates its own request syntax and storage field lengths before calling the connector.
Attachment protection spans setups using the same registered account and canonical logical path. Reuse that registration for shared attachment storage and keep path spelling consistent. Separate account registrations are separate scopes, even if they reach the same physical files; the interface exposes no physical identity or case-comparison contract.
Storage.File.Copy and Storage.File.Move require a destination that the connector reports as absent. An existing destination returns PreconditionFailed before a write. Linked moves require the storage implementation to guarantee source preservation on failure; the platform facade cannot provide that guarantee.

## Message types

| Area | Message type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Accounts | `Storage.Account.List` | Lists the configured storage connections. |
| Files | `Storage.File.List` | Lists the files in a folder. |
| Files | `Storage.File.Get` | Returns the content of one file as base64. |
| Files | `Storage.File.Exists` | Tells whether a file exists. |
| Files | `Storage.File.Create` | Writes a file from base64 content. |
| Files | `Storage.File.Copy` | Copies a file to a new path. |
| Files | `Storage.File.Move` | Moves or renames a file; a linked file keeps its attachment link. |
| Files | `Storage.File.Delete` | Deletes a file that no attachment uses. |
| Directories | `Storage.Directory.List` | Lists the subfolders of a folder. |
| Directories | `Storage.Directory.Exists` | Tells whether a folder exists. |
| Directories | `Storage.Directory.Create` | Creates a folder. |
| Directories | `Storage.Directory.Delete` | Deletes a folder that holds no linked file. |
| Attachments | `Storage.Attachment.Offload` | Moves the content of a document attachment to storage and links it. |
| Attachments | `Storage.Attachment.Restore` | Writes linked content back into the attachment. Deletes only a file newly created by that attachment; pre-existing files and legacy links are preserved. |
| Attachments | `Storage.Attachment.CreateLinked` | Attaches a stored file to a new or existing incoming document. Optional `dataExchangeType`, `process` and `vendorNo`. |
| Attachments | `Storage.Attachment.CreateForRecord` | Creates an attachment on a record from base64 content. |
| Uploads | `Storage.Upload.Begin` | Opens a chunked upload session. |
| Uploads | `Storage.Upload.Append` | Adds the next chunk to an open session. |
| Uploads | `Storage.Upload.Status` | Returns the state of a session. |
| Uploads | `Storage.Upload.Commit` | Assembles the chunks and writes the file to storage. |
| Uploads | `Storage.Upload.CommitToRecord` | Assembles the chunks and attaches the file to a record or incoming document. IncomingDocument accepts `dataExchangeType`, `process` and `vendorNo`. |
| Uploads | `Storage.Upload.CommitToDataExchange` | Assembles the chunks into a parsed Data Exch. entry of an import definition; optional `process` and `keepFileInStorage`. See `Help.DataExchange.Get`. |
| Uploads | `Storage.Upload.Abort` | Discards an open session and its chunks. |

## Chunked uploads

Use an upload session when a file is larger than one request can carry: `Storage.Upload.Begin`, then `Storage.Upload.Append` once per chunk in order, then `Storage.Upload.Commit`, `Storage.Upload.CommitToRecord` or `Storage.Upload.CommitToDataExchange`. `Storage.Upload.Begin` returns `chunkSizeHint` and `maxChunkBytes`. Files are written under the `bifrost-uploads/` root unless the request names a folder. A session belongs to the user who opened it.

To feed an incoming document: `Storage.Upload.Begin` → `Storage.Upload.Append` → `Storage.Upload.CommitToRecord` with `target` IncomingDocument and optional `dataExchangeType`, `process` and `vendorNo`. Wire the type first with `DataExchange.Type.Set`. Processing errors stay on the incoming document as `processErrors`; the commit still returns Success. A file already in storage uses `Storage.Attachment.CreateLinked` with the same parameters.

## Linked files

A stored file that backs a document attachment is protected. Deleting it and writing a create, copy, move or upload commit onto its path are refused with `PreconditionFailed`; use `Storage.Attachment.Restore` to bring the content back first.

## Errors

A refused call answers `status = Error` with `code`, `parameter`, `received`, `expected` and `nextStep` for every problem found, so all problems can be fixed in one retry.

`Storage.Directory.Delete` refuses the connection root path with `InvalidParameter` before the connector is called; name a folder below the root to delete.

## Permissions

Assign the `BIFROST Attach ori` permission set. The Data Exchange message types are described by `Help.DataExchange.Get` and need `BIFROST DataExch ori`.

data.markdown:
# Bifrost Attachments - Data Exchange message types

Run the Business Central Data Exchange Framework (Data Exch. Def, Data Exchange Type and Data Exch. entries) without the user interface: install definitions, import files into parsed entries, apply the mappings, and export records or payment journals to files in storage.

## Pipeline

1. **Install or discover** a definition: `DataExchange.Definition.Import` installs the standard definition XML (`storageCode` + `path`, `contentBase64` up to 1 MB, or a chunked `uploadId`; `overwrite`, `newCode`). `DataExchange.Definition.List` and `DataExchange.Definition.Get` show what exists; `DataExchange.Definition.Export` returns the header by default; `inline: true` adds the XML, and `storageCode` + `path`/`folderPath` writes the XML to storage. Both XML destinations may be requested. Storage writes refuse an existing file by default; overwrite: true explicitly allows replacement. Linked attachment files remain protected. External writes cannot be rolled back.
2. **Import** a file with a Generic Import or Payroll Import definition: `DataExchange.Import.Run` (`storageCode` + `path` of a stored file, which stays unchanged, or `contentBase64` up to 1 MB) or, for a large file, `Storage.Upload.Begin` -> `Storage.Upload.Append` -> `Storage.Upload.CommitToDataExchange` (`uploadId`, `dataExchDefCode`, optional `keepFileInStorage`). Both create a Data Exch. entry, run the definition reader and return `entryNo`, `lineCount` and `fieldCount`. A file the reader cannot read is refused and leaves no entry.
3. **Inspect** the parsed fields: `DataExchange.Entry.Get` (`entryNo`, paged `fields`), `DataExchange.Entry.List` for older entries.
4. **Process** the entry: `DataExchange.Entry.Process` runs the definition mappings and returns `targets[]` (table, inserted and modified counts, record SystemIds). Or send `process: true` on the import to do both in one call; the import is then committed first, and a processing error is returned in `processResult.errors` while the entry stays.
5. **Export**: `DataExchange.Export.Run` runs a Generic Export definition over `tableId`/`tableName` with `tableView`, or over `recordIds`, and delivers the file to storage (`storageCode` + `path` or `folderPath`) and/or `inline` (up to 1 MB). `DataExchange.PaymentExport.Run` exports a payment journal batch (`journalTemplate`, `journalBatch`) with the payment export format of its bank account, marks the lines as exported and delivers the bank file.
6. **Clean up**: `DataExchange.Entry.Delete` deletes an entry and its fields. Entries created by these types are also removed by the retention policy on Bifrost Data Exchange Entry (30 days by default).

Incoming documents are the other import path: wire a Generic Import definition that maps to the intermediate table with `DataExchange.Type.Set`, then send the file with `Storage.Upload.CommitToRecord` or `Storage.Attachment.CreateLinked` (`target` IncomingDocument, `dataExchangeType`, `process`). `DataExchange.Entry.Process` refuses intermediate-table mappings and points there. Bank statements are imported with `Finance.BankReconciliation.Create`.

## Which type do I need?

| I want to | Message type |
|---|---|
| Find a definition code | `DataExchange.Definition.List` |
| See how a definition maps columns to fields | `DataExchange.Definition.Get` |
| Install a definition from its XML | `DataExchange.Definition.Import` |
| Get a definition as XML, or only its header | `DataExchange.Definition.Export` |
| Remove a definition nothing uses | `DataExchange.Definition.Delete` |
| See which Data Exchange Types exist | `DataExchange.Type.List` |
| Bind a Data Exchange Type to an import definition | `DataExchange.Type.Set` |
| Import a stored file or small inline content | `DataExchange.Import.Run` |
| Import a large file sent in chunks | `Storage.Upload.CommitToDataExchange` |
| Write the parsed lines to the business tables | `DataExchange.Entry.Process` |
| Export records to a file | `DataExchange.Export.Run` |
| Create the bank payment file of a payment journal | `DataExchange.PaymentExport.Run` |
| List, read or delete entries | `DataExchange.Entry.List`, `DataExchange.Entry.Get`, `DataExchange.Entry.Delete` |

## Chaining

Every code a list returns is the exact value the next call expects: `code` from `DataExchange.Definition.List` or `codes[]` from `DataExchange.Definition.Import` goes into `code` of `DataExchange.Definition.Get`, `DataExchange.Definition.Export` and `DataExchange.Definition.Delete`, and into `dataExchDefCode` of `DataExchange.Type.Set`, `DataExchange.Import.Run`, `Storage.Upload.CommitToDataExchange`, `DataExchange.Export.Run` and `DataExchange.Entry.List`. `entryNo` from an import, an export or `DataExchange.Entry.List` goes into `DataExchange.Entry.Get`, `DataExchange.Entry.Process` and `DataExchange.Entry.Delete`. `storageCode` and `path` of an export go into `Storage.File.Get`. Codes are never trimmed, upper-cased or shortened; send them exactly as returned.

## Errors

A refused call answers `status = Error` with `code`, `parameter`, `received`, `expected` and `nextStep` for every problem found. A failure after a write (a reader or mapping error, a file over 1 MB with `inline`, a failed storage write) rolls the call back. Read `Help.Implementation.Get` (subject = the message type) for the full contract of one type.

## Permissions

Assign `BIFROST DataExch ori` with the Foundation API baseline. This role grants table read access, including the definition read by `DataExchange.Definition.Export`; it does not grant table writes. Definition.Export is registered Inbound because its optional storage output writes an external file; the storage connector also requires its own permissions.
The write types additionally require the standard Business Central permissions of the tables they write: Data Exch. and Data Exch. Field for imports and exports, the definition tables for `DataExchange.Definition.Import` and `DataExchange.Definition.Delete`, the target tables of the mappings for processing, and Gen. Journal Line and Credit Transfer Register for payment exports. Types with `storageCode` also use the storage connection. `BIFROST Attach ori` does not grant these Data Exchange table permissions.
